extracted.intended_audience: prospective creative-writing students and writers seeking workshops/courses (beginner to advanced)
extracted.subtask_description: A course-catalog-style listing of on-campus and online creative writing workshops and classes across genres (fiction, memoir, poetry, publishing, craft). Intended to help writers choose classes that target specific craft elements and professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program quality: expert instruction, individual attention, supportive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: What’s your story? Whether you’re just beginning to write or putting the finishing touches on your first novel, our on-campus and online writing courses offer expert instruction, individual attention, and supportive feedback at all levels, in all genres of creative writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotional statement functions as a program-level standard for course delivery: instructors should provide expert instruction, individual attention, and supportive feedback. Use this when evaluating the program or selecting courses; no further scoring guidance provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autofiction Workshop (Genealogy of the Spirit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Genealogy of the Spirit: Autofiction Workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course title indicates focus on autofiction — blending personal history and fiction; implies attention to voice, boundary between fact and invention, and personal narrative technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance novel craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting to the Heart of the Story: Romance Novel Workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the elements specific to romance novels — core emotional stakes ('heart of the story'), plotting for romantic arcs, and genre expectations for novel-length romance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative storytelling (SF & Fantasy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Art of Speculative Storytelling: Science Fiction and Fantasy Workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on speculative elements such as worldbuilding, plausibility of invented systems, and balancing idea-driven material with character and plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical fiction craft
rubrics_metrics.description: The Past Is Never Past: Historical Fiction Workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies standards like historical research, accuracy, integration of period detail, and handling historical perspective in narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting started in creative nonfiction / truth-telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting Started in Creative Nonfiction: A Ticket to the Truth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes approaching nonfiction with attention to 'truth' and ethical handling of real events/people; useful as a criterion for evaluating creative nonfiction pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir workshop / self and beyond
rubrics_metrics.description: The Self and Beyond: Memoir Workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets memoir-specific craft: shaping personal material into narrative, perspective, scope of self-representation, and moving beyond anecdote to thematic depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal essay: crafting resonance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights 'resonance' as a desired quality in personal essays — emotional truth, universality emerging from the particular, and craft choices that amplify impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of grief / generative writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Language of Grief: A Generative Writing Course
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on language choices for rendering grief, generative prompts to explore difficult emotional material, and attention to tone and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subplot mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastering Subplot in Novels and Memoirs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats subplot as a craft dimension to be managed: integration with main arc, pacing, thematic linkage, and sustaining reader interest across a long form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice in fiction: style, dialogue, and point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice in Fiction: Style, Dialogue, and Point of View
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly lists major voice components — style, dialogue, and POV — as evaluative criteria for fiction; guidance implies instruction on shaping and maintaining consistent, compelling voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene construction / 'Make a Scene'
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a Scene: The Essence of Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions the scene as the essential unit of storytelling; implies focus on showing vs telling, scene goals, beats, setting, and sensory detail to drive narrative forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel workshop: plot and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot and Structure: Novel Workshop for Manuscripts in Progress
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes structural elements of longer works: plot architecture, pacing over manuscript length, structural revisions, and readiness for manuscript-in-progress critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained narrative tension / 'writing you can't put down'
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing You Can't Put Down: Breakout Fiction Workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets techniques for reader engagement: momentum, stakes, cliffing, pacing, and hooks that sustain attention across a story or novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-form craft: flash fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash Fiction Workshop: Lightning on the Page
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights expectations for flash: compression, economy of language, striking image or twist, and maximal impact in minimal words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry craft as play / line technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry as Play: Poetry Workshop; How to 'Line Dance': Poetry Workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates poetic craft dimensions such as playfulness, lineation, formal choices, and experiments in sound/shape; 'line dance' suggests focus on line breaks and movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing a creative writing practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats regular practice as an evaluative/performance criterion: habit formation, generative techniques, productivity strategies, and sustaining a writing routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing readiness and pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Three Paths to Publishing: The Right Fit for Your Book; From Manuscript to Marketplace: A Publishing Intensive for Novelists and Memoirists; From Writer to Author: Navigating the Twisty Path to Publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames publishing as a set of professional standards: assessing the 'right fit' for a manuscript, preparing a manuscript for marketplace/readiness, and understanding routes (traditional, indie, hybrid). Useful when evaluating a work's suitability for market and next steps.
